hyps.why: Raising an already near-divergent learning rate hurts far more than raising it elsewhere.
Undertrained at tiny rates with a fixed epoch budget, so increasing the rate helps most.
Fewer update steps hurt most when the learning rate is already small.
More update steps compensate for slow learning at small rates.
Wider networks learn faster per step, helping when the rate is low.
Strong L2 already underfits, so more penalty hurts more than at small alpha.
Negligible regularization at small alpha makes an increase neutral or mildly helpful relative to high alpha.
Deeper networks are less stable at large learning rates.
Tiny batches combined with a high rate give noisy, unstable updates.
Wide layers with large rates are more prone to instability, reducing the benefit of added width.
